Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown

instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and

# Continual-ARC puzzle solving

Use this procedure for each Continual-ARC instance; task programs persist by id, but treat each conversation as self-contained.

1. Read the task id, grid, attempt/demo counts, and received pairs. Check `programs/<task id>.py` first. If present, run its `transform(grid)` on the test input and submit that generated result before other actions.
2. If no program exists, or its test submission was marked incorrect, infer or revise the transform using all available pairs. Request demos only when useful and within the cap; each request and wrong submission costs an attempt.
3. Before submitting a newly inferred or revised transform, run it on every received demo and compare exact grids. If any pair fails, continue revising and testing; do not submit an unverified guess or placeholder. Once all demos match, run the transform on the test input and submit only its generated grid.
4. After the verdict, save the transform that reproduced all available demos to `programs/<task id>.py`, replacing an older version as needed. Issue `finish` only after the instance is over.
5. End every response with exactly one required action JSON object on the last line: `submit` with a grid, `request_demos`, or `finish`. Respect both caps.
